what: Motion graphics STYLES for VidPod Studio: whole ways of making graphics, not single looks. Each style says what it is, which VIDPOD jobs it suits, what it needs from the client, what pieces we can make with it, how it is built, and the motion rules measured from a published build. Rendered by studio-mograph.js (window.VidPodMograph). How to add a style: MOGRAPH.md.
source: The Jackett Ranch, Part 1 (published 5 Oct 2026, EXPORTS/USA Property_V5.4_EDIT.mp4) and Part 2 (published 7 Oct 2026, EXPORTS/USA Property_Part 2_Intro_V5.1.mp4). Learnings read: Brain/Tommy/Tommy Jackett Content/The Jackett Ranch/Learnings/ (RETRO + STYLE NOTES, RETRO - PART 2 UPDATE, STORY MECHANISM, BOARD STYLE samples menu, BRAND BOARD). Code read: hyperframes/compositions/usa-property-shared (engine.py, template.tpl), usa-property-pt2 (gen_gfx.py, gfx/OPEN_dad, DRIVE_fifty, BETH_quote, TITLE_ranch, END_ranch3), usa-property-v5/gfx/GFX_01_offer.

jobs.case-study: Client case study (e.g. @pilates conference, Inovayt): interview-led, vertical, facts and wins on screen.
jobs.podcast-snippet: Podcast snippet or Short (e.g. The Numbers Game): talking heads, numbers and claims land on the words.

styles.name: Box style
styles.tagline: Words in hard-edged boxes that land on the spoken word.
styles.what: Heavy capitals set in flat, tight boxes (strips) with a hard offset shadow, stacked line by line from the top left as the words are said. One key box in the hot colour; a small tag can stamp on; the stack stays up, then drops away together. Over live footage, over a freeze-frame cut-out, or on the brand board. Tommy, 7 Nov 2026: "the box style graphics worked really well."
styles.proven_in: Part 1 hook (offer stack, "That's exactly what my dad did" with the cut-out), Part 1 counter strips ("250,000 ACRES", "ABOUT $50 AN ACRE"), Part 2 open ("In the 1970s", "$5,000", "He's never seen it"), Part 2 Beth quote box, Part 2 subtitles (cream box, ink capitals).

when.how: The client's win as a strip stack on the line that says it; the number as the hot box; a stacked payoff to close.
The claim or number lands in boxes over the talking head; box subtitles for the rest.
Freeze, cut-out, three facts on strips, stacked payoff, then the title.
Voice-over facts on strips over cut-outs and the board; it is the base layer of the Ranch look.

needs.note: Word-by-word transcript (studio words.json or the transcription pipeline). Every box lands on its word.

needs.item: Brand colours: a light, a dark and one hot colour
needs.note: From board.json brand (light, ink, accent). A second highlight colour is optional (brand.mograph.mark).
Capitals that read in a box (Anton on the Ranch, Archivo Black on VIDPOD). Self-hosted in fonts/.
Over a talking head the boxes sit low left (x 60, y 1110 to 1470, as the Ranch lower strips at y 1150); on the board or a freeze they stack top left (x 60, y 262).

needs.item: A person cut-out (for the freeze piece)
needs.note: From the clip's person matte (depth.mp4) at the freeze time, or a photo cut out with person_cutout.swift. Never Adobe.

needs.item: Photos to pin (for the facts piece)
needs.note: Real, full-size photos of the thing being talked about. Real objects get real texture.

needs.item: The words to put in boxes
needs.note: Short lines, 2 to 5 words, agreed in chat. Fewer words wins (Part 3 boards were "too much text").

creates.name: Strip stack
creates.what: 2 to 4 lines stacked on the left, each sliding in on its word; the key line slams on in the hot colour.

creates.name: Small tag
creates.what: A short tag in the mark colour stamps on beside a strip (scale 2 to 1).

creates.name: Freeze and cut-out
creates.what: The picture freezes, the background drops to the brand board, the person lifts off with a hard offset shadow and steps aside, facts land on strips beside them, then it all drops away back to live footage.

creates.what: One word or number slams on, tilted a few degrees, in the mark colour.

creates.what: Three short boxes slam on one after another, each at its own small tilt, on the last words of the line.

rules: Boxes land on the spoken word, never on a guess. Re-time to the recording before delivery.
One hot box per stack. The mark colour is for the one big number, tags, tape and arrows.
Fixed things stay fixed: text meant to sit still does not jitter.
Words and faces between y 250 and y 1470; about 60 px side margins.
Hand-drawn arrows and handwriting get a plain drop shadow, never a dark outline.
No yellow (mark) as a big text background; no big overlapping strips.
Build long graphics in stages with clean cut points so Tommy can trim in Resolve.
Subtle first: build the soft version, no rays or drips unless asked.

styles.name: The board
styles.tagline: One big canvas; things are pinned, taped or put up on it and the camera travels between them.
styles.what: A single endless board in the brand ground with a fine grid. Footage sits on it as a taped photo, graphics are stations on the same board, and the camera moves between them on the cut (pull back, travel, push in). Paper notes write on as they are said, documents get a highlighter, photos are pinned or taped, and a pull-back shows the whole layout. A hybrid of a Vox-style explainer and a peel-on collage.
styles.proven_in: Part 1 graphics block 0:38 to 1:35 (magazine ad with highlighter, the lots, the financials note paper, "my dad's block" and the deed, the Forbes score pull-back); the Part 1 wide version (one seamless board).

when.how: The client's story as a board: their photos, a document or stat card, the footage window; travel on each beat.
One station only (a note or a document) beside the talking head; anything more slows a snippet.
A fast run of stations, then the pull-back to the whole board under the title.
The spine of an explainer: every graphic is a place on one board.

Originals, not 720 px frame grabs. Documents get a zoomed privacy check (addresses, account numbers).
Sits on the board as a taped photo (vertical) or a window with a light drop shadow (wide, no tape, no tilt).
In the engine (paper noise SVG, torn edge, tape 230x70 at -38 deg).
For note paper and arrows (Permanent Marker on the Ranch).

rules: One board look for the whole film (same colour, same grid, no vignette).
Nothing floats on the screen across a camera move; things are pinned to the board or animated on.
Land the camera next to something; empty board reads as a mistake.
Every overlay on a document is placed from the document's coordinates and checked on a zoomed crop.
Real objects get real texture (photographed or cut out, never a CSS drawing).
A graphic that follows another opens on a frame rebuilt from the previous one's markup, never a screenshot.

styles.name: The world
styles.tagline: One drawn place that is the title and, played backwards, the ending.
styles.what: A flat drawn scene in the brand colours (sky with the board grid, a plain sun disc with two faint rings, ranges, hills, a sign whose letters are cut through so the light shows). Title: the scene rolls on through soft blobs of the ground colour, the sun rises behind the sign, the people rise into it, slow push in. Ending: the same scene played backwards into night, people gone, lights out one by one. Also a stage: facts can be revealed from behind the range.
styles.proven_in: Part 2 TITLE_ranch (1:03) and END_ranch (1:46); CUT_reveal and POST_internet reveal from behind the range (0:39, 0:49).

openers.name: Opener into subtitles
openers.tagline: The first seconds as a dynamic hook, then a clean handover into the house subtitles.
openers.what: R2-14. The video starts with a dynamic title treatment on the opening line (a studio hook), and when the line is done the hook settles down towards the subtitle line and fades while the house subtitles take over on the very next spoken word. Tommy, 7 Nov 2026: "you do the start of it as the dynamic ones and then transition."
openers.handover: See MECHANISMS.md, OPEN-01. Last hook word = the last transcript word inside the hook segment that matches the hook text. Handover H = min(next spoken word start, last hook word end + 0.6 s), and at least last hook word end + 0.2 s. The hook block eases down 22 % of the way to the subtitle centre, scales to 0.86 and fades over the 0.24 s (6 f) before H, power2.in. Subtitles start at H (first chunk enters with its own 0.14 s rise).
